results.name: Elbow before you swing
results.headline: Small change needed: 10° away from the target
results.cue: Your arm is too straight behind you before you swing, so the swing is slow. Bend your elbow more before you swing.

drills.name: Shadow smash with a pause
drills.purpose: Getting your racket arm ready behind your head, with your side to the net.
steps: Stand side-on to the net, racket up.
Lift the racket behind your head with your elbow up and bent like the letter L. Stop for 2 seconds.
Turn your chest to the net and swing, finishing with the racket across your body.

results.name: Reaching up to hit
results.headline: Small change needed: 8° away from the target
results.cue: You hit the shuttle with a bent arm, so it does not go down sharply. Reach up and hit it with a straight arm.

drills.name: Highest-point contact
drills.purpose: Hitting the shuttle as high as you can reach, so it goes down sharply.
steps: Hang a shuttle on a string just above your full overhead reach, or have a partner hold one up.
Practise your smash and touch the shuttle with the racket, arm fully straight.
Raise it a little once you can reach it every time.

results.name: Racket arm speed
results.headline: Small change needed: 115° per second away from the target
results.cue: Your arm is moving slowly. Keep your arm relaxed. In badminton, speed comes from a quick, relaxed arm, not from force.

drills.name: Fast swings with the cover on
drills.purpose: A relaxed, fast lower arm and wrist.
steps: Put the head cover on your racket. This makes it a little harder to swing.
From the ready position, swing with a relaxed grip and let your lower arm turn over fast.
Listen for the whoosh sound. A louder whoosh means a faster swing.
drills.equipment: A racket with a head cover
drills.safety: Hold the racket gently. Stop if your elbow or shoulder hurts.

results.name: Knee bend before you jump
results.headline: Almost right: 3° away from the target
results.cue: You hardly bend your knees, so only your arm is working. Bend your knees and jump. Hitting from higher sends the shuttle down sharply.

drills.name: Scissor-kick jumps
drills.purpose: Bending your knees and jumping up, with your hips turning first.
steps: Start side-on with your racket-side leg back.
Bend your legs, jump, and swap legs in the air like a scissor.
Turn your hips first, then your shoulders, then swing. Land balanced.
drills.safety: Land with soft knees. Skip if your knees or ankles hurt.

results.name: Hips and chest come up together
results.headline: Small change needed: 28 ms away from the target

drills.name: Box squats
drills.purpose: Going low enough every time, with your hips and chest coming up together.
steps: Put a box or bench behind you at a height where your thighs are about level with the floor when you sit.
Squat down until you just touch it, without dropping onto it.
Stand up with your chest and hips rising at the same speed. Use a higher or lower box to change how low you go.

drills.name: Slow squats
drills.purpose: A slow, steady squat with both legs working equally.
steps: Bodyweight only. Take 3 seconds to go down, pause 1 second, and take 1 second to come up.
Watch your knees in a mirror. They should stay above your toes, both the same.
Keep your weight even across both feet.

results.name: Keeping your back flat
results.headline: Almost right: 4° away from the target
results.cue: Your lower back curves at the bottom of the squat. This is the most risky mistake in a squat. Do not go so low, and tighten your stomach before you go down.

drills.name: Goblet squats with a pause
drills.purpose: A chest that stays up and a flat lower back at the lowest point.

Squat down, keeping your chest up and back flat, and pause 2 seconds at the bottom.
Stand up slowly. Do not go lower than the point where your lower back starts to curve.

steps: Start side-on with your racket-side leg back.
Bend your legs, jump, and swap legs in the air like a scissor.
Turn your hips first, then your shoulders, then swing. Land balanced.
drills.safety: Land with soft knees. Skip if your knees or ankles hurt.

results.name: Hips turn first, then shoulders
results.headline: Almost right: 12 ms away from the target
results.cue: Your hips and shoulders turn at the same time, so you lose power. Turn your hips first, then your shoulders, then your arm.

results.name: Turning your body
results.headline: Almost right: 3° away from the target
results.cue: You face the net and do not turn your body, so only your arm is working. Stand side-on to the net, then turn as you hit.

drills.name: Shadow smash with a pause
drills.purpose: Getting your racket arm ready behind your head, with your side to the net.
steps: Stand side-on to the net, racket up.
Lift the racket behind your head with your elbow up and bent like the letter L. Stop for 2 seconds.
Turn your chest to the net and swing, finishing with the racket across your body.

results.name: Elbow before you swing
results.headline: Needs practice: 15° away from the target
results.cue: Your arm is too straight behind you before you swing, so the swing is slow. Bend your elbow more before you swing.

drills.name: Shadow smash with a pause
drills.purpose: Getting your racket arm ready behind your head, with your side to the net.
steps: Stand side-on to the net, racket up.
Lift the racket behind your head with your elbow up and bent like the letter L. Stop for 2 seconds.
Turn your chest to the net and swing, finishing with the racket across your body.

results.name: Reaching up to hit
results.headline: Needs practice: 12° away from the target
results.cue: You hit the shuttle with a bent arm, so it does not go down sharply. Reach up and hit it with a straight arm.

drills.name: Highest-point contact
drills.purpose: Hitting the shuttle as high as you can reach, so it goes down sharply.
steps: Hang a shuttle on a string just above your full overhead reach, or have a partner hold one up.
Practise your smash and touch the shuttle with the racket, arm fully straight.
Raise it a little once you can reach it every time.

results.name: Racket arm speed
results.headline: Small change needed: 185° per second away from the target
results.cue: Your arm is moving slowly. Keep your arm relaxed. In badminton, speed comes from a quick, relaxed arm, not from force.

drills.name: Fast swings with the cover on
drills.purpose: A relaxed, fast lower arm and wrist.
steps: Put the head cover on your racket. This makes it a little harder to swing.
From the ready position, swing with a relaxed grip and let your lower arm turn over fast.
Listen for the whoosh sound. A louder whoosh means a faster swing.
drills.equipment: A racket with a head cover
drills.safety: Hold the racket gently. Stop if your elbow or shoulder hurts.

results.name: Knee bend before you jump

results.cue: You hardly bend your knees, so only your arm is working. Bend your knees and jump. Hitting from higher sends the shuttle down sharply.
